original_value: Image fusion has emerged as a major area of research in the past few decades due to its extended applications. While progressing in the field of image fusion, a large number of techniques‐based image transforms and spatial filters have been devised for both general and specific sets of images. The primary criterion of image fusion technique is to deliver high‐quality visual perception besides giving a considerable objective evaluation rate. In this study, an information fusion rate‐based study is done on recent, most researched, and high‐performing state‐of‐the‐art techniques using visible and infrared image datasets. These techniques have been chosen carefully, owing to their superiority in performance on both objective and subjective scales of evaluation and have been discussed in terms of their respective advantages and disadvantages. It is clearly evident that some rather primitive techniques can perform well as well as techniques based on a hybrid of various domains can significantly boost the information fusion rate.

result.paraphrase: Image fusion has become an important research area over the last few decades because of its wide range of applications. As the field has advanced, many transform- and spatial filter-based methods have been developed for both general and specialized image sets. The main goal of image fusion techniques is to provide strong visual quality while also achieving a high objective evaluation score. This study presents an information fusion rate-based analysis of recent, widely studied, and high-performing state-of-the-art methods using visible and infrared image datasets. These methods were selected with care for their superior performance on both objective and subjective evaluation measures, and their strengths and weaknesses are discussed. It is clear that even some relatively basic techniques can perform well, and that hybrid methods combining multiple domains can substantially improve the information fusion rate.
